::: {#rem-cross-entropy-loss}
#### Why models are fit by minimizing cross-entropy

Fitting a classifier by minimizing [cross-entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-cross-entropy)
chooses the [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $q$ the model assigns
so that a code built for $q$ would spend as few [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) as possible
on the observed labels.
By @rem-cross-entropy-wrong-code, that pushes $q$
toward the probabilities the labels came from.

For a single labeled example,
let $e$ put all its mass on the observed label.
Then $\entropyf{e} = 0$
([as for a coin that always lands heads](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#exm-entropy-coin)),
so the example's cross-entropy $\crossentropyf{e}{q}$ equals $\kldivf{e}{q}$:
every [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit) it reports is a wasted one.

:::
